info.title: API Curupira
info.description:
Curupira API: the collection schedule by neighborhood, anonymous environmental reports with photo and map, and the management panel for the city team.

The site (`/storefront`) answers without a session. Everything else requires the `httpOnly` cookie `curupira-access-token`, issued by `POST /authentication/sign-in` and renewed by `POST /authentication/refresh`.

Every failure returns the same body: `{ message, status, code, errors? }`, where `code` is the machine identifier and `errors` maps field to message when the failure is per field.

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description: Sign in, sign out and session renewal. The token pair travels in an `httpOnly` cookie, so these routes answer `204` with no body - what matters is the `Set-Cookie`.

tags.name: Account
tags.description: The account itself, whatever the role. No identifier in the path: the scope comes from the session, never from the payload - whoever edits is always whoever is authenticated.

tags.name: Attachments
tags.description: Upload in three steps, because the binary does **not** cross this application: `POST` opens and returns signed URLs, the browser uploads the parts straight to the bucket, and `complete` confirms against the real object. The record is born without an owner - whoever attaches keeps the reference.

tags.name: Management · Reports
tags.description: The environmental reports for the team: list with filters, map pins, dashboard numbers, detail with the contact and signed photos, and the status moving forward. Operators and administrators.

tags.name: Management · Notices
tags.description: The notices the home shows between two dates. Operators and administrators.

tags.name: Management · Collection schedule
tags.description: The weekly collection slots: a waste type, weekday and shift in a neighborhood. Administrators only.

tags.name: Management · Neighborhoods
tags.description: The neighborhoods residents pick, with an optional center on the map. Administrators only.

tags.name: Management · Users
tags.description: The access accounts: administrators and operators. There is no public sign-up - every account is born here. The password is never returned in any response. Administrators only.

tags.name: Site · Neighborhoods
tags.description: The neighborhood list the resident picks from. **Unauthenticated**.

tags.name: Site · Collection schedule
tags.description: The week of collection, per neighborhood. **Unauthenticated**.

tags.name: Site · Report photos
tags.description: Anonymous photo upload for a report, in two steps: open (signed `PUT`) and confirm, which verifies the image and strips its metadata. **Unauthenticated**, throttled per IP.

tags.name: Site · Reports
tags.description: File a report anonymously, follow it by protocol and see the public map. The public reads never carry the contact, the description or the photos. **Unauthenticated**, throttled per IP.

get.description:
The own account, whatever the role. The user always comes from the session: there is no identifier in the path, and there could not be - the scope comes from the token, never from the payload.

The avatar comes preloaded, with the `url` derived at serialization.

422.description: Invalid data · Senha atual inválida · A nova senha deve ser diferente da atual · Arquivo não encontrado

put.description:
Every field is optional: only what comes in the payload changes. A missing field means "leave alone", not "erase" - the exception is `avatarId`, where `null` is how the photo is removed without replacing it.

Changing the password requires `currentPassword`, the current password: the session proves possession of the cookie, not identity, and without it a hijacked cookie would change the account owner's password. The new password must still differ from the current one.

Changing email or password **revokes all sessions**, including the one that made this request.

The role is not accepted: it is set at creation, by the administrator, and nobody changes their own.

post.description:
Refreshes the session from the refresh cookie, and responds `204` with the new token pair in `Set-Cookie`.

It sits **outside** the authenticated group on purpose: it is precisely the expired access token that brings someone here, so requiring a valid session would make the route unreachable. What authorizes is the refresh cookie, and nothing else.

**Rotates**: the used refresh is deleted when the new one is issued. Two simultaneous refreshes with the same token spend it twice, and the second drops the session.

A missing, unreadable or non-refresh cookie responds `401`, without distinguishing which of the three it was.

Opens the session. Responds `204` **without a body**: what matters is the `Set-Cookie` with the `httpOnly` token pair. The client never handles the token, and no user data travels inside it.

The failure is **indistinguishable by cause**: wrong password and inactive account return the same `401`. That is what prevents discovering, from the response, which emails exist.

Ends the session **on the server**, not just on screen: deletes the current access token and the refresh token, then clears both cookies. Responds `204` without a body.

An unreadable refresh token does not prevent sign-out - the cookies are cleared anyway, because the result the person asked for is to be without a session.

It deletes only the tokens of this session. Dropping **all** of them is a consequence of changing email or password in `PUT /account`, not of this route.

`?sort` accepts title, startsAt, createdAt. Default: the most recent start first.

Publishes a notice on the home between `startsAt` and the optional `endsAt`. A start in the future schedules it.

`endsAt` must be after `startsAt`: otherwise `422`.

Ends the showing now: the notice leaves the home immediately and its status becomes `CLOSED`. It stays in the panel list.

Closing twice responds `409`.

Paginated listing for the panel, with the neighborhood name. Cuts: `?kind`, `?status`, `?neighborhoodId`, `?from`/`?to` (ISO 8601 instants) and `?search` (protocol or description).

`?sort` accepts createdAt, status, kind. Default: the most recent first.

The contact and the description are only in the detail (`GET /management/reports/:id`).

get.description: Totals by kind and by status (every key present, even at zero) and the reports created per day over the last 30 days (every day present). Days follow the city time zone (America/Manaus).

403.description: Access denied. Requires one of these roles: ADMINISTRATOR, OPERATOR.

get.description:
The full report for the panel: description, contact (when the resident left one), photos with a short-lived signed `url`, and the whole timeline with who answered.

The contact is personal data and exists only here, behind the panel roles.

403.description: Access denied. Requires one of these roles: ADMINISTRATOR, OPERATOR.

delete.description:
**Irreversible**: removes the report, its timeline and its photos (row and binary). The protocol stops resolving on the public page.

Meant for spam and test reports; a handled report is kept and moved to RESOLVED.

patch.description:
Advances the status (RECEIVED, IN_REVIEW, FORWARDED, RESOLVED) and writes a timeline event with the author and the optional `message`, which the resident reads on the protocol page.

The status only moves forward - to a later one, skipping steps if needed. Going back or repeating responds `422`.

Registers that a waste type is collected in a neighborhood on a weekday and shift. The same neighborhood, type, weekday and shift cannot be registered twice: it responds `409`.

An unknown `neighborhoodId` responds `422` pointing at the field.

get.description:
Paginated listing. `?role` and `?status` are the two cuts of the screen, and `?search` filters by name and email.

The password does not come out here nor in any API response.

`?sort` accepts name, email, createdAt and `?direction` accepts asc or desc. Default: page 1, 20 per page, ordered by name ascending.

422.description: Invalid data · Senha atual inválida · A nova senha deve ser diferente da atual

post.description:
Returns `201` with the created account, bare object, without envelope and **without the password**.

The only way to create a user in the API: there is no public sign-up, and the first owner comes from the seeder.

`role` is required - the role is always explicit on the server. `password` requires `passwordConfirmation` with the same value.

The email of another account responds `409`.

403.description: Access denied. Requires one of these roles: ADMINISTRATOR.

403.description: Access denied. Requires one of these roles: ADMINISTRATOR.

422.description: Invalid data · Senha atual inválida · A nova senha deve ser diferente da atual

put.description:
Every field is optional: only what comes in the payload changes. A missing field means "leave alone", not "erase".

Changing email or password, changing the role or deactivating **drops all sessions** of the changed account - without that, switching someone's access off would switch nothing off. The response never carries the password.

On the **own** account, `role` and `status` respond `403`: demoting oneself or marking oneself `INACTIVE` removes from the panel whoever was administering. Name, email and password remain editable.

403.description: Access denied. Requires one of these roles: ADMINISTRATOR.

delete.description:
**Irreversible**: deletes the account, and with it its tokens in `auth_access_tokens` by `CASCADE` - a token is a live credential, and leaving it behind would keep a session that nobody can revoke anymore.

The history the account wrote on reports stays, with no author. To only switch the access off, set `status` to `INACTIVE` on `PUT /management/users/:id`.

The **own** account responds `403`.

get.description:
The panel file library. `?search` filters by original name, generated name and type, `?status` separates what has already been uploaded from the open upload, and `?mimetype` narrows to one type only.

`?mimetype` accepts image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, image/gif, application/pdf, audio/mpeg, audio/mp4, audio/ogg, audio/wav.

`?sort` accepts originalName, mimetype, size, createdAt and `?direction` accepts asc or desc. Default: page 1, 20 per page, from most recent to oldest - in a file library what matters is what has just been uploaded.

post.description:
Opens an upload and returns where to upload it. **Does not receive bytes** - only the metadata of the file.

The binary goes from the browser straight to the bucket, by signed URL, and never crosses this application: a large file in an HTTP body hits the proxy limit, occupies the application for the duration of the upload, and cannot be resumed when the connection drops.

Accepts image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, image/gif, application/pdf, audio/mpeg, audio/mp4, audio/ogg, audio/wav, up to 1073741824 bytes, refused **before** any signature: a forbidden file gets no URL, so it never reaches the bucket. That the declared size is true is what `POST /storages/:id/complete` checks, against the real object.

The file is sliced into parts of 10485760 bytes. When it fits in a single part, `uploadId` is null and the only URL accepts a `PUT` with the whole file. When it does not fit, each URL accepts its part, the client keeps the `ETag` each `PUT` returns, and `parts` may carry only the first batch - the rest comes from `GET /storages/:id/parts`, which is the same endpoint as the resume.

The row is born `PENDING` and cannot be attached to anything until it is confirmed. The file is born without an owner: whoever attaches keeps the reference, informing the `id` in the resource field (today, the user `avatarId`).

get.description:
Returns the bare record, without envelope: the original label, the type, the size, the state of the upload and the derived `url`.

Also valid for a file still `PENDING` - the detail screen is where one discovers that an upload was left half-done. Whoever attaches is the one who requires `UPLOADED`.

422.description: Invalid data · Arquivo incompleto · Arquivo incompleto

delete.description:
**Irreversible**: deletes the binary in the bucket and the row in `storages`.

Only deletes an **orphan** file. The file is a neutral, shared record - it does not belong to the form that submitted it -, so whoever references it rules: a file in use by another record (today, a user avatar) responds `409`, with the origin in the message. Unlink first, delete after.

A file still `PENDING` is an upload cancellation: the multipart is aborted, and that is what makes the parts already sent disappear from the bucket.

It is the pair of `POST /storages`, which saves the file before the form is saved: without this route, every attachment chosen and then removed from the screen would stay in the bucket forever.

422.description: Invalid data · Arquivo incompleto · Arquivo incompleto

post.description:
Closes the upload opened by `POST /storages`: the bucket reassembles the parts and the row becomes `UPLOADED`, the only state that can be attached to anything.

The body carries the `ETag` each part `PUT` returned - that is how the storage verifies that no part was lost or arrived half-written. A single-part upload has no part to confirm, and `parts` is absent.

This is where the size **declared** in `POST /storages` is compared with that of the object that actually arrived. If it diverges, the object is deleted, the row dies with it and the response is `422`. The `mimetype` is not checked because it cannot diverge: it goes into the signature of the URL, and the bucket refuses a `PUT` that does not match it.

Calling twice is safe: the second returns the same record.

get.summary: Download file with the original name
get.description:
Redirects to a temporary bucket URL that delivers the file with `Content-Disposition: attachment` and the original name.

It exists because of a browser limitation, not a storage one: the `download` attribute of an `<a>` is ignored across origins, and the API answers on an origin different from the app. Without this route, "save file" would open the image in a tab, and the file would arrive named with the uuid instead of the name the person uploaded.

It redirects instead of serving the binary: the header travels signed inside the URL, so the application hands out an address and gets out of the way, instead of being busy for the duration of each download transfer.

**Requires a session**: the bucket is `visibility: private`, and while this route was open it issued a signed URL for any uuid without a session - the back door the closing of the bucket left open. A file the person cannot reach responds `404` and not `403`, so as not to confirm to a prober that the uuid exists.

Where to continue from: in `uploaded`, what the bucket has already received; in `parts`, a new URL for what is missing.

It serves two cases that are the same problem. **Resume**: the connection dropped midway, and without this the only way out would be to start over. **Next batch**: the URLs come out 100 at a time, because signing everything at once would be hundreds of kilobytes of JSON before the first byte goes up. Each part has 10485760 bytes.

Signing again is the point, not a side effect: a signed URL expires, and an upload that lasted longer than the validity finds here a new address for the same part.

An already confirmed file responds `200` with both lists empty - whoever asks is a resuming client, and reading the `status` and stopping is the right outcome.
Every neighborhood, by name, in the pagination envelope but on a single page: the resident picks theirs from a short list. Public.
The notices showing right now (status ACTIVE), the most recent start first. Scheduled and closed ones never appear here. Public.

post.description:
Opens the upload of one photo for a report and returns where to `PUT` it. **Does not receive bytes**: the photo goes straight to the bucket by a signed URL that expires in 15 minutes.

Only `image/jpeg`, `image/png` and `image/webp`, up to the configured ceiling, refused **before** any signature. Then call `POST /storefront/report-photos/:id/complete`. Public, throttled per IP.

422.description: Invalid data · A foto enviada não é uma imagem válida · Arquivo incompleto · Arquivo incompleto

post.description:
Closes the upload: checks that what arrived has the declared size and really is the declared image type, **strips every embedded metadata** (EXIF, GPS, XMP) re-encoding the image, and only then marks it `UPLOADED` so a report can attach it.

The report location comes from the form pin, never from the photo: nothing in the stored file tells where it was taken.

A file that fails any check is deleted and responds `422`. Calling again on a confirmed photo is safe (`204`). Public, throttled per IP.

409.description: Não foi possível gerar o protocolo. Tente novamente

422.description: Invalid data · Arquivo não encontrado · O status só pode avançar · Uma das fotos já foi usada em outra denúncia

post.description:
Files an environmental report. **Anonymous**: no session, and the report is anonymous unless `contact` is sent (the server derives that, the client does not declare it).

The response is only the `protocol` (`CUR-XXXX-XXXX`), the one key to follow the report on `GET /storefront/reports/:protocol`. The location comes from `latitude`/`longitude`; the neighborhood is matched to the nearest one with a center, when there is one.

`photoIds` are photos confirmed by `POST /storefront/report-photos/:id/complete`, from 1 to 3, each used by a single report. Public, throttled per IP.

get.description:
The pins of the public map: only reports already looked at (IN_REVIEW, FORWARDED, RESOLVED), so a hoax or a misplaced pin never shows before someone reviewed it.

Each pin carries the kind, status, coordinates **rounded to about 110 m** and the **day** (no hour). The newest 500 only. No text, no contact, no protocol, no photo. Public.

The status page of a report, with no session: protocol, type, status, creation date and the timeline (status, the answer text and the instant of each step).

**Never** the contact, the description, the photos, the coordinates or who answered. The protocol is normalized (case, spaces, hyphens, look-alike letters). An unknown or malformed protocol responds the same `404`. Public, throttled per IP.
The whole week, with no page: every slot, in week order (Sunday first) and then by shift. `?neighborhoodId` cuts to one neighborhood. Public.
